content.text:
**No repo files have been changed.** I understand the vision as:

> Hunchlane helps someone research an idea, decide what to build, create it, deploy it, and keep improving it—all within the same product.

Hunchlane itself is a good sample because it lets visitors see how we evaluate our own idea. My proposed report title is **“Hunchlane: from an uncertain idea to a working product.”**

One adjustment: the report should explain **why Hunchlane could win, where competitors are stronger, and what would prove our approach works**. Research cannot honestly establish that Hunchlane will succeed and others won’t.

The initial research gives us this competitive picture:

| Alternative | Verified offering | Question for Hunchlane |
|---|---|---|
| Lovable | Builds, deploys, hosts, and manages products; also offers planning before implementation. | Can research meaningfully improve what gets built? |
| Replit | Conversational app creation, integrations, testing, and launch from one workspace. | Can Hunchlane guide an uncertain founder better? |
| DimeADozen | Sourced business-validation reports; advertises a $9 starter and $129 full report. | Can Hunchlane turn findings into measurable action? |
| ValidatorAI | Free idea analysis, competitive insights, and a next-step prompt for building a landing page or site. | Does keeping the entire process inside Hunchlane produce better outcomes? |

Sources: [Lovable](https://lovable.dev/), [Lovable planning](https://docs.lovable.dev/features/plan-mode), [Replit Agent](https://replit.com/products/agent), [DimeADozen](https://www.dimeadozen.ai/), [ValidatorAI](https://validatorai.com/).

**The strongest proposed differentiation is continuity between evidence and execution.** For example, the report identifies a customer problem; Hunchlane turns that finding into a small product; the deployed product measures whether customers actually experience and pay to solve that problem. Those results then inform the next version. This is a hypothesis worth testing, rather than an established market gap.

I propose the full sample contains:

1. **The idea and first customer:** begin with nontechnical solo founders exploring a small web product. Clearly label this audience as our proposed starting point.
2. **The market and alternatives:** sourced capabilities, overlap, pricing where verified, and fair reasons someone might choose each competitor.
3. **Why Hunchlane could work:** less repeated explanation, research that shapes the build, smaller experiments before expensive development, and ongoing learning after launch.
4. **Why it could fail:** users may want immediate building; research may feel generic; existing builders may offer comparable guidance; development, hosting, and support costs may undermine the business.
5. **The product journey:** idea → research → customer experiment → build → deploy → manage → improve. Future capabilities must be visibly labeled as planned.
6. **The numbers:** an assumption model covering research costs, build costs, hosting, support, pricing, and repeat usage. No invented revenue forecasts or CFO.ai results.
7. **A first validation test:** help ten target founders compare a report-only experience with a guided report-to-prototype experience. Measure completion, time, willingness to pay, and whether they return. Any success thresholds would be chosen in advance and labeled as our test criteria.
8. **Evidence and unanswered questions:** dated sources, claim-level citations, assumptions, and missing customer evidence.

The landing preview would condense this into three pages: **What already exists → Hunchlane’s possible advantage → How we test it.** The sample page would carry the full report.

**Do you approve this direction before I prepare the complete sample and make repo changes?**
